他走了 28 年回到家，妈妈开门只问了一句：“你去哪儿了？”He walked home for 28 years. His mum opened the door and asked, “Where have you been?”

卡尔·布什比，一个把“回家”走成五万公里的人。我想把他讲给你听——不是因为他励志，而是因为他把一件事做了 28 年。Karl Bushby turned “going home” into a 50,000-kilometre walk. I want to tell you about him — not because he’s inspiring, but because he did one thing for 28 years.

文 · 忽晚（镜中虚梦）By 忽晚 (镜中虚梦)发布于 2026 年 11 月 7 日 23:40Published 7 November 2026, 23:40人物 · 探险People · Adventure
一分钟版本：1998 年 11 月 1 日，29 岁的英国退伍伞兵卡尔·布什比从智利最南端的蓬塔阿雷纳斯出发，给自己定了两条规矩——不坐任何交通工具往前推进，没走完就不回英国。他穿过达连地峡的雨林，2006 年徒步跨越白令海峡的浮冰，被俄罗斯遣返后跟签证耗了十年，2024 年用 31 天游过里海，2026 年 10 月 5 日游过英吉利海峡，11 月 2 日走进赫尔的家门。10,227 天，约 5 万公里。The short version: on 1 November 1998, Karl Bushby — a 29-year-old former British paratrooper — set off from Punta Arenas, at the southern tip of Chile, with two rules: never let transport move the line forward, and don’t set foot back in the UK until it’s finished. He crossed the Darién Gap, walked the Bering Strait ice in 2006, spent a decade fighting paperwork after being deported from Russia, swam the Caspian Sea in 31 days in 2024, swam the English Channel on 5 October 2026, and walked into his mother’s street in Hull on 2 November. 10,227 days. About 50,000 kilometres.

2026 年 11 月 2 日，英格兰赫尔，一条再普通不过的居民街。有户人家的窗户上挂着横幅：“Welcome Home Son — from your 28 year adventure”。门口挤着邻居、记者、举手机的人，还有一支纪录片摄制组。On 2 November 2026, on a completely ordinary residential street in Hull, England, a banner hung in a window: “Welcome Home Son — from your 28 year adventure.” Neighbours, reporters, people holding up their phones and a documentary crew were packed outside the door.

门开了。79 岁的安吉拉走出来，抱住她 57 岁的儿子，哭得几乎站不稳。她问：The door opened. Angela, 79, came out and put her arms around her 57-year-old son, sobbing so hard she could barely stand. She asked:

“你去哪儿了？”“Where have you been?”

他不用回答。这个问题，他用了 28 年、五万公里、四个大洲、大约三十个国家来回答。He didn’t need to answer. He had spent 28 years, 50,000 kilometres, four continents and roughly thirty countries answering it.

这个人叫卡尔·布什比（Karl Bushby）。今天想把他讲给你听，是因为我翻完他的故事之后，发现它最打动我的地方，恰恰不是“一个人有多强”，而是另外一件很轻的事——他在路上靠的全是陌生人的善意。His name is Karl Bushby. I want to tell you about him because, after reading through his story, what moved me most wasn’t how strong one man can be. It was something much lighter: he got through it almost entirely on the kindness of strangers.

0 1一张生日贺卡A birthday card

故事开始于 1990 年代中期一张生日贺卡。The story starts with a birthday card in the mid-1990s.

寄卡的是他父亲基思。老爷子在军队待了 24 年，其中 12 年在特种部队。贺卡上没写什么人生道理，只提了一件小事：两个特种兵在争论，人能不能从伦敦出发，沿着白令陆桥，一路走到纽约。It came from his father, Keith — 24 years in the army, 12 of them in special forces. The card had no life advice in it. It mentioned one small thing: two special forces soldiers arguing about whether a person could walk from London, across the Bering land bridge, all the way to New York.

就这么一句话。That was it. One sentence.

布什比当时二十几岁，在伞兵团服役——他在部队待了 11 年，是合格的空降兵，习惯了“走路、负重、把自己撑到底”这一套。他退伍后过着普通日子，直到看见这句话。Bushby was in his twenties, serving in the Parachute Regiment — 11 years in uniform, a qualified paratrooper, used to walking, carrying weight and pushing himself to the limit. He left the army and lived an ordinary life, until he read that line.

他拿起笔，在世界地图上画了一条线：从英国出发，穿过欧洲、亚洲，越过白令海峡，穿过北美，一路向南，直到南美洲最南端。He picked up a pen and drew a line across a world map: out of Britain, through Europe and Asia, over the Bering Strait, across North America, all the way down to the southern tip of South America.

然后他决定，反着走一遍，走回家。Then he decided to walk it in reverse — and walk home.

他给这件事起名叫“歌利亚远征”（Goliath Expedition）。歌利亚是《圣经》里那个巨人——意思是，这是一个大得不成比例的东西。He called it the Goliath Expedition. Goliath is the giant from the Bible — the point being that this was something absurdly, comically big.

“我活在父亲的影子里。他不只是当了 24 年兵、12 年特种部队，他还是个拿过顶级考核的伞兵。”“I lived in the shadow of my father. Not only 24 years in the army and 12 years special forces, but an ex-paratrooper who had received top P Company recruit.”

—— 卡尔·布什比— Karl Bushby

0 2两条铁律Two rules

1998 年 11 月 1 日，智利蓬塔阿雷纳斯。29 岁的布什比带着大约 500 美元出发。1 November 1998, Punta Arenas, Chile. Bushby, 29, set off with about 500 dollars.

出发前他给自己定了两条规矩：Before leaving, he gave himself two rules:

第一，不能用任何交通工具“推进”路线。可以走，可以游，可以等，但不能坐车、坐船、坐飞机往前挪一米。One: no vehicle may advance the route. He could walk, swim or wait — but he couldn’t move a single metre forward by car, boat or plane.

第二，没走完之前，不回英国。Two: no going back to the UK until it was done.

这两条规矩听起来像少年意气。但后面 28 年所有的痛苦，几乎都是它们带来的。The rules sound like youthful bravado. But almost every hardship of the next 28 years came from them.

他原本估计 5 年能走完。后来他自己说：“你只要把一整桶现实倒在这上面……我们猜的是 12 年以上。而那个‘以上’，是个很大的‘以上’。但我们做梦也没想到是 28 年。”He originally guessed five years. Later he put it this way: “You just dump a whole bucket full of reality on that... We suspected that it was 12 years plus. And the plus was a big plus. But never in our wildest dreams would we ever have imagined 28 years.”

0 3前半程：雨林、沙漠、冰The first half: jungle, desert, ice

1998 到 2006，他用了八年，从南美走到阿拉斯加。From 1998 to 2006 he spent eight years getting from South America to Alaska.

最凶的一段是达连地峡——哥伦比亚和巴拿马之间那片没有公路的雨林。毒贩、地方武装、沼泽、鳄鱼，还有能把人皮肤泡烂的湿热。2001 年他穿了过去，随后在巴拿马因为进入限制区域，被关了 18 天。The worst stretch was the Darién Gap — the roadless jungle between Colombia and Panama. Drug traffickers, armed groups, swamps, crocodiles, and heat wet enough to rot your skin. He crossed it in 2001 and was then jailed for 18 days in Panama for entering a restricted zone.

然后是中美洲、墨西哥、美国西部、加拿大、阿拉斯加。零下四十度的夜里，他拖着那辆被自己叫作“野兽”（the Beast）的行李车。车坏了就修，修不了就找人重做——后来的第二辆，是尼加拉瓜一所技术学校按他的要求焊出来的。Then came Central America, Mexico, the western United States, Canada, Alaska. In temperatures of minus forty he dragged the cart he called “the Beast”. When it broke he fixed it; when he couldn’t, he had it rebuilt — the second one was welded to his specifications at a technical college in Nicaragua.

真正的关隘在白令海峡。The real gate was the Bering Strait.

2006 年 3 月，他和美国探险者迪米特里·基弗（Dimitri Kieffer）一起，用 14 天走过 90 公里的浮冰。冰在漂，裂缝随时张开，人被洋流带着偏离航线；冰碎了就下水游，水温接近零度。中途他们被直升机接走过一次，又回到原地重新开始。他们还和一头北极熊对峙过，雪橇掉进海里，差点丢掉全部补给。In March 2006 he crossed 90 kilometres of drifting ice with the American adventurer Dimitri Kieffer in 14 days. The ice moved, cracks opened without warning, currents pushed them off course; when the ice broke they swam, in water close to zero. Halfway through they were airlifted out once, then went back and started again. They faced down a polar bear, and their sleds went into the sea, nearly taking all their supplies with them.

他们成了极少数徒步穿越白令海峡的人。They became one of the very few pairs to walk across the Bering Strait.

然后俄罗斯把他们抓了——非法入境。拘留，罚款，遣返。Then Russia arrested them — illegal entry. Detained, fined, deported.

0 4真正的敌人是签证The real enemy was paperwork

如果故事到这里是“人战胜自然”，那接下来的十年就是“人对抗表格”。If the first half was man against nature, the next ten years were man against forms.

俄罗斯只给他 90 天的旅游签。走到期限，他就得飞出去，再飞回来，从上次停下的那个点继续走。Russia gave him 90-day tourist visas. When one ran out he had to fly out, fly back in, and resume from the exact point where he had stopped.

2008 年金融危机，赞助商全没了。他停了三年。In 2008 the financial crisis wiped out his sponsors. He stopped for three years.

2012 年，俄罗斯拒绝给他新签证，还给了五年禁令——理由是当年穿越白令海峡在技术上属于违规。In 2012 Russia refused him a new visa and handed him a five-year ban — on the grounds that the Bering crossing had technically broken the rules.

他的回应是：从洛杉矶出发，徒步 3000 英里走到华盛顿的俄罗斯大使馆，站在门口抗议。His response was to walk 3,000 miles from Los Angeles to the Russian embassy in Washington and protest outside it.

后来禁令撤销。2014 年，他重新拿到签证，回到俄罗斯，接着走。The ban was later lifted. In 2014 he got a visa, went back to Russia and carried on.

2020 年，疫情让全世界停了下来。一个以“不停”为生的人，只能等在原地。In 2020 the pandemic stopped the world. A man who lived by not stopping had to stand still.

2022 年，战争封死了他原本要走的路。In 2022 the war closed the route he had planned.

28 年里，他真正在走路的时间大约只有 15 年。剩下的时间在等签证、等天气、等钱、等一张纸。Of those 28 years, he spent only about 15 actually walking. The rest went on visas, weather, money and pieces of paper.

0 5一个不擅长游泳的人，游过了里海A man who can’t really swim, crossing the Caspian

原路走不通，他决定从哈萨克斯坦游到阿塞拜疆，横渡里海。The old route was gone, so he decided to swim from Kazakhstan to Azerbaijan — across the Caspian Sea.

2024 年 8 月末到 9 月，31 天，288 公里，累计在水里超过 132 小时。同行的有探险者安吉拉·马克斯韦尔、一名阿塞拜疆游泳运动员和一支海上保障队。From late August to September 2024: 31 days, 288 kilometres, more than 132 hours in the water. With him were the adventurer Angela Maxwell, an Azerbaijani swimmer and a support team at sea.

他不擅长游泳。这不是一句修辞——一个不擅长游泳的人，为了不违背“不坐船”的规矩，把自己泡在海里一个月。He is not a strong swimmer. That’s not a figure of speech — a man who can’t really swim spent a month in the sea rather than break the rule about boats.

2024 年 11 月，他从巴库上岸，继续向西。2025 年 4 月，他走到伊斯坦布尔，重新回到欧洲。In November 2024 he came ashore at Baku and kept heading west. In April 2025 he reached Istanbul, back in Europe.

2026 年 10 月 5 日，他游过英吉利海峡，在多佛附近的莎士比亚海滩上岸。他的父亲和兄弟在沙滩上等他。On 5 October 2026 he swam the English Channel and landed at Shakespeare Beach near Dover. His father and brothers were waiting on the sand.

0 6最后 400 公里The last 400 kilometres

从多佛到赫尔，大约 400 公里。这是 28 年里最短、也最不像“探险”的一段。Dover to Hull is about 400 kilometres — the shortest, least adventurous leg in 28 years.

10 月 28 日，有人拍到他在林肯郡的乡间公路上推着车走。两个骑摩托的人停下来，冲他竖起大拇指。On 28 October someone filmed him pushing his cart along a country road in Lincolnshire. Two motorcyclists pulled over and gave him a thumbs up.

11 月 2 日上午，他推着那辆“野兽”走过亨伯桥。陪着他的是 79 岁的父亲基思和 54 岁的弟弟阿德里安。赫尔市中心的维多利亚女王广场聚了几百人，市长在市政厅门口迎接他。On the morning of 2 November he pushed the Beast across the Humber Bridge. With him were his father Keith, 79, and his brother Adrian, 54. A few hundred people gathered in Queen Victoria Square in Hull city centre, and the Lord Mayor welcomed him at the City Hall.

他对着人群开玩笑：“抱歉让你们久等了。就这样？结束了吗？”He joked to the crowd: “Sorry to keep you waiting. Is that it, is it done?”

然后他继续往北走，走到母亲家门口。Then he carried on north, to his mother’s front door.

“他们说要养大一个孩子，需要一个村庄。但说实话，把我送回家的是整个世界。陌生人的善意，太多太多了，从一个人到一个国家。我不是一个人走完的。我有一支很大的队伍。最大的那支。地球。”“They say it takes a village but literally it took a world to get me here. The kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation states to get me back here today. I didn’t do this alone. There was a big team. The biggest team. Earth.”

—— 卡尔·布什比，2026 年 11 月 2 日— Karl Bushby, 2 November 2026

母亲抱住他，问：“你去哪儿了？”His mother hugged him and asked, “Where have you been?”

他后来在发布会上说，这个瞬间他在路上想象过很多次，但真的发生时，“是一大团模糊的东西”，他还在慢慢消化。“这么久之后再见到我母亲，有点震惊。她变了很多。我们都变了很多。”At a press conference later he said he had imagined the moment many times on the road, but when it happened it was “one great, big, blurry mess” he was still trying to process. “It was kind of almost shocking to see my mother after so long. She’s changed a lot. We’ve all changed a lot in that time.”

0 7账单The bill

10,227

公里km

个国家countries

出发时他 29 岁，刚经历一场婚姻破裂，儿子亚当还很小。回家时他 57 岁，儿子 36 岁，孙女 12 岁——他第一次见到她，就在回家的那几天。He left at 29, recently divorced, with a small son, Adam. He came home at 57: his son is 36, his granddaughter is 12 — and he met her for the first time in the days around his return.

他和母亲有十年没见。He hadn’t seen his mother in a decade.

他在路上说过一句话：“我们本不该这样生活。”On the road he said: “We’re not supposed to live like this.”

他还说过，回家有点像“跨过事件视界掉进黑洞”，不知道接下来会发生什么。他得先住进母亲家的地下室，重新适应英国商店里的商品，重新学着做一个儿子、一个父亲、一个普通人。He also said coming home felt like “stepping across the event horizon into a black hole” — not knowing what happens next. He would be living in his mum’s basement, relearning British shops, relearning how to be a son, a father, an ordinary person.

  • 199811 月 1 日，智利蓬塔阿雷纳斯出发，29 岁，约 500 美元。1 Nov. Leaves Punta Arenas, Chile — 29 years old, about $500.
  • 2001穿越达连地峡，在巴拿马被关 18 天。Crosses the Darién Gap; jailed for 18 days in Panama.
  • 20063 月，14 天徒步 90 公里跨越白令海峡，随后在俄罗斯被拘留遣返。March. Walks 90 km across the Bering Strait in 14 days; detained and deported by Russia.
  • 2008金融危机，赞助中断，停滞三年。Financial crisis; sponsors vanish; three years stalled.
  • 2012俄罗斯拒签并下五年禁令；他从洛杉矶徒步 3000 英里到华盛顿抗议。Russia refuses a visa and bans him for five years; he walks 3,000 miles from LA to Washington to protest.
  • 2014重新拿到俄罗斯签证，继续向东走。Gets a Russian visa and carries on.
  • 2020疫情，边境关闭，原地等待。Pandemic; borders close; he waits.
  • 20248–9 月，31 天 288 公里横渡里海；11 月从巴库上岸。Aug–Sep: swims the Caspian — 31 days, 288 km; lands at Baku in November.
  • 20254 月，抵达伊斯坦布尔，回到欧洲。April. Reaches Istanbul, back in Europe.
  • 202610 月 5 日游过英吉利海峡；11 月 2 日走进赫尔，10,227 天，结束。5 Oct. Swims the English Channel; 2 Nov. walks into Hull. 10,227 days. Done.

0 8我为什么想把他讲给你听Why I want to tell you about him

我们太熟悉那种“挑战极限”的叙事了：登顶、穿越、破纪录，然后下山、回家、出书。布什比的故事是反过来的。We know the “conquering the limit” story too well: summit, cross, break the record, come down, go home, write a book. Bushby’s story runs the other way.

他的“极限”不是某一座山，而是时间本身。他最难的关卡不在荒野，在签证窗口。他赢的方式不是某一次爆发，而是 10,227 天里，每一天都没有让那条线断掉。His limit wasn’t a mountain. It was time. His hardest obstacle wasn’t wilderness, it was a visa window. And he didn’t win with one big push — he won by not letting the line break, for 10,227 days.

而且他诚实地说了代价。他没有把这 28 年包装成纯粹的浪漫：他错过了儿子的成长，让母亲等了十年，回家后要住进母亲家的地下室。他说自己像一个只为这件事存在的人，然后这件事结束了。And he’s honest about the bill. He doesn’t sell the 28 years as pure romance: he missed his son growing up, he kept his mother waiting a decade, and he came home to his mum’s basement. He became a man who existed for one thing — and then the thing ended.

他现在有六场演讲要讲，回忆录《Giant Steps》要写续集，导演沃纳·赫尔佐格要给他拍纪录片。He now has six speaking engagements booked, a sequel to his memoir Giant Steps to write, and Werner Herzog wants to make a documentary about him.

但我最喜欢的，还是他到家时那句玩笑。But my favourite line is the joke he made when he arrived.

28 年，五万公里，就为了能站在自家门口，说一句“我回来了”。Twenty-eight years. Fifty thousand kilometres. All so he could stand at his own front door and say: I’m home.

如果你最近也在做一件很久才看得到结果的事——把这篇存下来。
有人做了 28 年。If you’re in the middle of something that will take a long time to show results — save this one.
Somebody did it for 28 years.
